title: Fold Digits Down to Two
statement:
You get a string s of decimal digits. One fold replaces it with a string one digit shorter: the new digit at position i is (s[i] + s[i + 1]) mod 10.

Keep folding until exactly two digits are left. Return true if those two digits are equal, and false otherwise.
hints: The length is small. Just do what the statement says and fold until two digits remain.
Each fold builds a new array of length one less, using (a + b) % 10. You can also overwrite the array in place, left to right.
Bonus: the final left digit is a weighted sum of the original digits with Pascal's triangle as the weights, mod 10. Where have you seen that triangle before?

explain.intuition:
This is a direct simulation. A string of length n needs n − 2 folds, and fold number k touches about n − k digits, so the total work is about n² / 2, tiny for 100 digits. Folding in place works if you go left to right: d[i] is overwritten only after it has been used for the new d[i], and d[i + 1] is still the old value.

There is a pattern underneath. After all the folds, the left digit is Σ C(m, i) · d[i] mod 10 with m = n − 2, the same weights as row m of Pascal's triangle. The right digit uses the same weights shifted by one. That view is what makes a much longer version of this problem solvable.
steps: Turn s into an array of digits.
While the array is longer than 2: for i from 0 to length − 2, set d[i] = (d[i] + d[i + 1]) % 10, then drop the last element.
pitfalls: Folding right to left in place. Then d[i + 1] has already been replaced by its new value when you use it.
Stopping at one digit instead of two, or folding once too few.
Forgetting the mod 10, so digits grow into multi-digit numbers.

solutions.title: Fold in place
solutions.idea: Overwrite the digit array left to right on each fold and shorten it by one.

solutions.title: Pascal weights
solutions.idea: Build row n − 2 of Pascal's triangle mod 10. The two final digits are weighted sums of the original digits with those weights, one shifted by a position.

followups: The string can now have 100 000 digits. How do you get C(m, i) mod 10 for one row without building the whole triangle? (Hint: work mod 2 and mod 5 separately.)
Why does the left-to-right in-place fold never read a value it has already overwritten?
